value.body: Bachelor of Siddha Medicine and Surgery. Siddha is a traditional system of medicine from Tamil Nadu. You study modern medical basics alongside Siddha principles, pharmacology and external therapies such as varmam, then complete a one-year internship. It is regulated by the National Commission for Indian System of Medicine (NCISM).

items.label: Course length
items.note: 4½ years of study + 1-year compulsory rotatory internship

items.label: UG seats
items.note: Across 17 colleges permitted for 2025-26 (list as on 29 Aug 2025); approx. sum
items.source: NCISM list of permitted Siddha colleges, approx.

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Class 12 with Physics, Chemistry and Biology, and a qualifying NEET-UG score. AACCC (Ministry of Ayush) counsels the 15% All India Quota and central, national-institute and deemed-university seats; states fill the rest through their own counselling. In Tamil Nadu, students who have not studied Tamil up to Class 10 or 12 study it in the first year.

value.title: At a glance
items: 16 of the 17 permitted Siddha colleges are in Tamil Nadu; one is in Kerala.
Practice needs registration with a State Board or Council of Indian Medicine.
An MD (Siddha) through AIAPGET is the usual way to specialise.
